data.title: Go World Travel Magazine Wins Bronze for Best Editorial Travel Website in the 2026 SATW Foundation Lowell Thomas Travel Journalism Competition
data.description:
Go World Travel Magazine Wins Bronze for Best Editorial Travel Website in the 2026 SATW Foundation Lowell Thomas Travel Journalism Competition

Go World Travel Magazine Wins Bronze for Best Editorial Travel Website in the 2026 SATW Foundation Lowell Thomas Travel Journalism Competition

PR Newswire

ARVADA, Colo., Oct. 9, 2026

ARVADA, Colo., Oct. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Go World Travel Magazine (GoWorldTravel.com) has won the Bronze award for Best Editorial Travel Website in the 2026 Lowell Thomas Travel Journalism Competition, sponsored by the Society of American Travel Writers Foundation (SATW Foundation). The awards were announced on October 6 at the SATW annual convention in Haywood County, North Carolina.

Go World Travel shares the honor with two other leading travel publications: BBC Travel won Gold and Azure Road won Silver. Go World Travel was recognized under the leadership of Managing Editor Janna Graber.

"We're thrilled and honored by this recognition," said Graber. "We believe travel connects people, and our goal is to inspire readers to explore the world with curiosity and respect. This award belongs to our talented team of editors, writers and photographers."

About the Lowell Thomas Travel Journalism Competition

Named for pioneering broadcaster, author and world traveler Lowell Thomas, the Lowell Thomas Competition is widely regarded as the premier travel journalism competition in North America. The SATW Foundation has sponsored it since 1984 and today awards more than $25,000 in prize money each year for print, digital, multimedia and broadcast work. The competition does not promote any destination or travel product, has no membership requirement for entrants, and is judged independently by journalism faculty.

This year, 26 judges at the University of Missouri School of Journalism reviewed 1,568 entries and gave 120 awards.

About Go World Travel Magazine

Go World Travel Magazine is an independent digital travel magazine for curious, culturally minded travelers. The digital magazine shares destination features, cultural stories, and practical travel advice from writers and photographers around the globe, publishing daily stories on travel in more than 90 countries. Through its coverage, Go World Travel seeks to foster cross-cultural understanding and help readers travel more meaningfully, engaging with local communities and returning home with a deeper sense of shared humanity. Learn more at GoWorldTravel.com.

About the SATW Foundation

The Society of American Travel Writers Foundation was founded in 1984 to honor outstanding work in travel journalism. It is a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization whose mission is to support, celebrate and sustain excellence in travel journalism that serves the public. Full results are available at satwfoundation.org.

data.title: AHF Champions Girls’ Health, Rights and Futures on International Day of the Girl
data.description:
AHF Champions Girls’ Health, Rights and Futures on International Day of the Girl

On International Day of the Girl, observed annually on Oct. 11, AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) is calling for greater action to ensure girls everywhere have the health, education, protection, and opportunities they need to thrive and reach their full potential.

Despite decades of progress, major barriers continue to limit girls’ opportunities. HIV continues to disproportionately affect girls in many parts of the world. In 2025, girls accounted for more than two-thirds of all new HIV infections among adolescents globally. In sub-Saharan Africa, almost six times as many adolescent girls acquired HIV as adolescent boys. Additionally, an estimated 133 million girls globally did not attend school in 2024. These disparities reinforce the need to ensure they have access to accurate sexual and reproductive health information and HIV prevention, testing, and treatment services that allow them to make informed decisions about their lives and health.

Child marriage remains another serious threat to girls’ health, education, and independence. Each year, 12 million girls are married before age 18. Child marriage also makes it difficult for girls to negotiate safer sex with their husbands, who are often older, leaving them especially vulnerable to HIV and other sexually transmitted infections, gender-based violence, and limited access to services and information.

“Every girl deserves the freedom to grow up healthy, stay in school and make her own decisions about her future. But millions of girls are still being denied those opportunities because of inequality, violence, child marriage, and barriers to health care and education,” said Loretta Wong, AHF Deputy Chief of Global Advocacy & Policy. “We must give girls the knowledge, resources, and support to protect their health, develop their potential, and lead change in their lives and communities. This includes championing policies and services that are responsive to the health needs of young people. We urge governments, communities, families, and civil society to break down these barriers that continue to hold girls back.”

AHF advances those goals through Girls Act, its global girl-led empowerment program that builds leadership, confidence, and life skills among girls and young women. Launched in 2016, AHF operates Girls Act programs in 37 countries across Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, and the Caribbean. The program focuses on HIV and STI prevention, supporting girls living with HIV to stay on treatment, reducing unplanned pregnancies, keeping girls in school, and strengthening advocacy, leadership, and peer support.

International Day of the Girl reminds us that empowering girls today creates healthier, stronger, and more equitable communities for generations to come.

AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF), the world’s largest HIV/AIDS healthcare organization, provides cutting-edge medicine and advocacy to more than 3.3 million people across 50 countries, including the U.S. and in Africa, Latin America/Caribbean, the Asia/Pacific Region, and Eastern Europe. In January 2025, AHF received the MLK, Jr. Social Justice Award, The King Center’s highest recognition for an organization leading work in the social justice arena. To learn more about AHF, visit us online at AIDShealth.org, find us on Facebook, and follow us on Instagram, Twitter, and TikTok.

data.title: Tata Motors Raises Bid for Italy's Iveco
data.description:
By Joshua Kirby 




  Tata Motors raised its offer for Iveco in light of delays due to regulatory approvals, pushing up the value of the planned takeover closer to just shy of 4 billion euros ($4.49 billion.) 



  India's Tata Motors said in a filing published Friday that it raised its offer to 14.40 euros a share, up 30 cents from the original 14.10 euros it had offered for the truck maker. The new offer gives the company an equity value of around 3.905 billion euros, according to the filing. Shares in Milan-listed Iveco closed Friday around the new offer level of 14.40 euros. 



  Iveco said last month its board unanimously supported the initial offer, and recommended shareholders accept the deal. The company said Friday it welcomed the increase in the offer price. 



  Tata Motors, an arm of conglomerate Tata Group that counts British luxury auto maker Jaguar among its assets, agreed last year to buy Iveco's commercial-vehicles business, with the completion of the transaction subject to the spinoff of Iveco's defense business. Italy's Leonardo agreed to buy that business earlier this year, paving the way for the takeover of the remaining business by Tata Motors. 



  Shareholders will vote on the transaction at a meeting scheduled for Oct. 16.

SPT Investor Alert: Robbins LLP Announces that Sprout Social, Inc. Beat Motion to Dismiss

Shareholder rights law firm Robbins LLP informs investors that on October 6, 2026, the plaintiffs in the class action against Sprout Social (NASDAQ: SPT) beat defendants' motion to dismiss the complaint. Accordingly, the stay of the case was lifted and the parties are to submit a proposed schedule for the completion of fact and expert discovery.

The class action was initially filed on behalf of persons and entities that purchased or otherwise acquired Sprout Social securities between November 2, 2023 and May 2, 2024, inclusive (the "Class Period").

Why Was Sprout Social Sued?

According to the class action complaint, during the Class Period, defendants failed to disclose to investors: (1) the Company’s sales and revenue growth were not indicative of the Company’s growth as it transitioned to an enterprise sales cycle; (2) that the Company faced integration challenges with its acquisition of Tagger; (3) as a result, the Company was “self inducing sales headwinds;” and (4) as a result, the Company would revise fiscal year 2024 revenue guidance.

On May 2, 2024, Sprout Social announced the Company’s operating results for the first fiscal quarter of 2024, disclosing that the Company had missed its revenue guidance for the quarter, and revising its full year 2024 revenue guidance downward $20 million. The Company’s Chief Financial Officer Joe Del Preto stated the Company had “underestimated the magnitude of enterprise seasonality” and that the Company had also been “self-inducing sales execution headwinds.” On this news, Sprout Social’s stock price fell $19.33, or 40.1%, to close at $28.82 per share on May 3, 2024.

data.title: More evidence that broad-market index funds remain unbeatable, even in the era of AI stock-picking
data.description:
By Mark Hulbert

Two out of three large-cap funds lagged the S&P 500 in the first half of the year

There's plenty of evidence that, if you were to pick a mutual fund at random, the odds are high that it will lag the S&P 500.

Picking market-beating stocks has not become any easier this year, according to the latest S&P Dow Jones Indices report on mutual-fund performance.

For the first six months of this year, according to the company's recent report, 67% of large-cap domestic equity funds underperformed the S&P 500 SPX. That's almost precisely the average extent of underperformance in each of the past 25 years.

These findings put to rest the widespread speculation from earlier this year that, because market leadership in the first half of the year was rotating away from the largest-cap stocks represented by the so-called "Magnificent Seven" tech companies, a greater percentage of mutual funds should beat the market. That's because the S&P 500 is a market-cap-weighted index and its performance disproportionately suffers when its largest stocks perform poorly.

This argument had at least superficial plausibility, since for the first half of this year the average Magnificent Seven stock lost 3.1%, according to LSEG data. Yet beating the market was still difficult: The percentage of mutual funds lagging the S&P 500 was virtually no different in the first half of this year than the past 25 years' average.

The new report from S&P Dow Jones Indices also puts to rest the argument that AI would lead to a greater percentage of mutual funds beating the market. That's not the case, despite AI's use becoming widespread on Wall Street. A March survey from Mercer found that "55% of asset managers report AI is integrated in at least one of their strategy's investment processes, 27% are at pilot/proof-of-concept, and only 18% report no integration yet." If AI made it easier to pick market-beating stocks, we therefore should have seen a much lower percentage this year of mutual funds lagging the market. But as you can see from the chart, AI has made no detectable difference.

This year's results provide yet more evidence that, if you were to pick a mutual fund at random, the odds are high that you will lag a broad-market index fund.

But what if the best mutual funds are able to repeat?

The standard comeback to this conclusion is that we don't have to pick a mutual fund at random, but can instead pick those that have the best past performance. If those best performers have above-average odds of continuing their winning ways, do we really care that the majority of funds are losers?

We wouldn't care - if last year's best performer had an above-average chance of beating the market this year. But that is not the case. We know that because of the very high percentage - over 90% - of mutual funds that have lagged the S&P 500 for cumulative performance over the past 20 years. This is represented by the green line in the above chart. That line would be significantly lower if there were greater persistence in mutual funds' ranks in the yearly performance scoreboards.

The bottom line: Yet again, we see that it's incredibly difficult to beat a simple strategy of buying and holding a broad stock-market index fund. If you can't beat the benchmark even when it is handicapped by the lagging performance of the biggest stocks, and even with AI becoming as widely used as it has been, what makes you think the odds will be any better in the future?

Mark Hulbert is a regular contributor to MarketWatch. His Hulbert Ratings tracks investment newsletters that pay a flat fee to be audited. He can be reached at mark@hulbertratings.com

-Mark Hulbert

data.title: Elon Musk is now richer than any American ever - and it's not even close
data.description:
By Christine Ji

Musk's trillioniare status means he's wealthier than his next three contemporaries combined - and also worth more than historical tycoons like John D. Rockefeller

A rally in SpaceX and Tesla shares sent Elon Musk's net worth back above the trillion-dollar mark.

Recent gains in shares of SpaceX and Tesla have pushed Elon Musk's net worth back beyond the trillion-dollar mark.

Musk's wealth has earned him the title of the world's first and only trillionaire - and the richest person in the history of America by certain measures, surpassing the wealth of industrialists like John D. Rockefeller and Andrew Carnegie when looking relative to economic output.

As of Thursday, Musk's net worth was $1.02 trillion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. The majority of Musk's wealth comes from his stakes in SpaceX (SPCX) and Tesla (TSLA), two companies with multi-trillion-dollar market capitalizations. Since the beginning of the month, shares of both companies have risen 6%.

Musk holds a 48.4% equity stake in SpaceX, which represents approximately 6.42 billion shares across common stock, options and unvested performance awards, according to an August SEC filing. Musk also owns 20% of Tesla, according to a June SEC filing. However, wealth calculations typically exclude the value of unvested performance shares. Musk also owns shares of his private companies Neuralink and the Boring Co.

These positions make Musk's net worth highly volatile. His wealth peaked at $1.32 trillion in June following SpaceX's IPO but then fell below $700 billion in August as those shares lost ground.

Despite these fluctuations, Musk has solidly established himself as the wealthiest person in the world, both now and compared to previous eras.

Musk's current net worth makes him richer than the world's next three wealthiest individuals - Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) co-founder Larry Page, Amazon.com (AMZN) founder Jeff Bezos and and Google co-founder Sergey Brin - combined.

Musk has spent the majority of the past five years in the top position since first overtaking Bezos in 2021. Musk's current trillionaire status is also a testament to how much the ceiling for wealth has expanded in the past few years. In 2020, Bezos became the first person to ever cross the $200 billion mark. In April 2025, Musk's net worth of $342 billion made him the wealthiest person in the world. In the 18 months since, Musk's net worth has nearly tripled.

Musk also remains peerless when compared to the richest Americans in history.

The industrialists of the 19th and 20th centuries made their fortunes on new markets like oil, steel and railroads. Today, the artificial-intelligence boom has drawn comparisons to the Industrial Revolution in terms of the transformative potential of the technology. While the economic impact of AI has yet to fully emerge, Musk has already surpassed the richest Americans in history in terms of his relative share of gross domestic output.

MarketWatch identified comparable historic figures from Forbes' 2007 list of the richest Americans of all time, then calculated each individual's peak net worth as a percentage of U.S. GDP at the time. Those historical GDP shares were then applied to today's economy.

Note: Historical wealth estimates are approximate and may not represent individuals' exact peak fortunes. Carnegie's figure reflects proceeds from the sale of his steel business.

U.S. GDP reached an annualized $32.56 trillion in the second quarter ending Sept. 30. That means Musk's fortune equates to roughly 3.1% of the entire national economy - a higher percentage than any American before him.

Measuring historic wealth by modern-day standards is challenging because the underlying economic conditions have changed drastically. Additionally, readers should note that historical net-worth estimates are often debated due to differences in record-keeping and varying valuation methods. With that being said, economists typically measure historic wealth as a share of GDP instead of adjusting by standard consumer price inflation.

For example, Standard Oil founder John D. Rockefeller has long been considered the richest American in history. Rockefeller was worth $900 million at his peak in 1913, according to biographer Ron Chernow. Adjusted for inflation, his fortune would be worth $30.4 billion today. But when compared to U.S. GDP in 1913 - which was $39.5 billion, according to Measuring Worth - Rockefeller's wealth comprised 2.3% of total national output, or the equivalent of roughly $742 billion in today's economy.

Andrew Carnegie is believed to have given away $350 million, or roughly 90% of his fortune, over his lifetime. But to pinpoint his net worth at a specific point in time, MarketWatch used the 1901 buyout of Carnegie Steel to J.P Morgan as a benchmark for his peak wealth. While the exact amount is debated, PBS claims Carnegie walked away from the transaction with $250 million, earning him the title of the richest man in the world at the time. The proceeds of the sale represented 1.1% of U.S. GDP at the time, or the equivalent of $355 billion today.

-Christine Ji

data.title: The Week in Oil: Escalating Middle East Attacks Threaten Supply Recovery
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni 




  Here is a look at what happened in oil markets in the week of Oct. 5-9 and what the focus will be in the days to come. 





  OVERVIEW: Oil prices are on track for a weekly gain despite retreating earlier in the session after President Trump said the U.S. wouldn't attack Iran before the midterm elections, citing "productive" talks with Tehran. Brent crude, the global benchmark, trades around $104 a barrel, while WTI futures hover near $92. 





  MACRO: Escalating attacks in the Middle East continue to sustain a high geopolitical risk premium in oil prices, with many analysts anticipating prolonged supply disruptions into early 2027. At the same time, markets are increasingly focused on the inflationary implications of higher energy prices and their potential impact on the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy path. Renewed concerns that persistent energy-driven inflation could prompt further monetary tightening have shifted interest-rate expectations, with CME's FedWatch tool indicating a 19% probability of a rate hike in October and an 86% probability in December. 





  GEOPOLITICAL RISKS: Oil prices have climbed sharply over the week, with Brent crude above $105 a barrel on fears of military escalation in the Middle East. Supply concerns have intensified amid an increase in Iranian attacks on vessels in the Persian Gulf and Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia. While exports flows had recovered at around prewar levels, analysts at Kpler say recent attacks have driven flows sharply lower this week: confirmed total oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz dropped sharply to 2.72 million barrels a day on Oct. 7 from 12.26 million barrels a day on Oct. 4. 



  In the U.S., a hurricane has forced some major producers to shut down production on the Gulf Coast, putting at risk key refineries in the region and threatening to further tighten an already constrained market for refined oil products. 





  SUPPLY AND DEMAND: A recent recovery in exports shouldn't be mistaken for a return to normal market conditions, analysts say. Shipping costs remain exceptionally high, and significant refining capacity across the Middle East is still offline. As a result, supplies of refined products remain tight and prices elevated, particularly for middle distillates such as diesel, jet fuel and heating oil. 



  The G7's announcement of a 100-million-barrel release of crude oil and diesel initially eased market concerns, but the impact has since faded as it became clear that some of the volume reflected the acceleration of previously planned releases rather than additional supply. Moreover, strategic reserves can provide only temporary relief; they can't repair damaged refineries or restore disrupted distribution networks, says Ole Hansen from Saxo Bank. 





  WHAT'S AHEAD: Next week, attention will turn to fresh oil-market data, with OPEC and the International Energy Agency set to publish their monthly reports. The IEA's assessment of global inventories will be particularly important following last week's announcement of emergency oil stocks. 



  China's trade data will also be closely watched, especially crude oil imports and refined-product exports. Beijing has helped ease market tightness by reducing crude imports while increasing product exports, and any change in this trend could have significant implications for the global supply outlook, analysts at Commerzbank said. 



  On the U.S. economic calendar, focus will turn to CPI inflation data due on Wednesday and PPI figures due on Thursday for more cues on the interest-rate path this year.

data.title: Flu season is already here. Here's what to know about this year's flu shots.
data.description:
By Jaimy Lee

There are several options for flu shots, including the first mRNA flu vaccine, which was developed by Moderna

There are several options for flu shots this year, including a new mRNA-based flu vaccine developed by Moderna and Sanofi's Fluzone, which is available as a regular shot and as a high-dose version for people over 65.

The flu season has arrived earlier than expected this year.

The rate of flu-related visits to a doctor's office, emergency room or hospital for the week ending Sept. 13 was double what it was last year at the same time, according to Epic Research, which gathers data from hospitals that use Epic for their electronic medical records. That translates to the flu season landing about seven weeks earlier than in 2025 or 2024.

The Epic data, which was published Thursday, show that the flu is hitting states like Alaska, Hawaii, Florida, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas the hardest. The drugstore chain Walgreens has seen a double-digit jump in sales of cold and flu medications as well as cough drops, according to a report in ABC News.

"For people who are there, I'm telling people: 'Get your flu shot ASAP,'" said Celine Gounder, an infectious-disease doctor and editor at large for public health at KFF Health News. "For everybody else, before the end of the month. We have this expression: Flu before 'boo' for Halloween."

There are several flu shots available this year, including Moderna's (MRNA) mFLUSIVA, a new mRNA-based shot that's approved for Americans who are at least 50 years old. When compared with GSK's (GSK) Fluarix, Moderna's vaccine produced higher antibody titers, according to a small study that evaluated the two vaccines in 75 people in the U.S. and that was recently published in Nature Immunology.

The mFLUSIVA vaccine is more effective than other flu shots, although it comes with more side effects, which are similar to what people experience with Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine.

There are also the standard options available like CSL Seqirus's Fluad, which is approved for older adults; AstraZeneca's (AZN) FluMist, a nasal spray that is approved for children and adults younger than 50; and Sanofi's (FR:SAN) Fluzone, which is available as a regular shot and as a high-dose version that has been cleared for use in people over 65. All available flu shots in the U.S. are trivalent vaccines, meaning they help protect against H1N1, H3N2 and B/Victoria.

This year's flu season may be worsened by a mutation in the H3N2 strain, particularly in people younger than 25, according to Gounder. Flu rates are also rising early in other parts of the Northern Hemisphere, such as Japan and the U.K.

-Jaimy Lee

data.title: Apply for the Sonic Impact Scholarship Program By October 31
data.description:
Apply for the Sonic Impact Scholarship Program By October 31

Apply for the Sonic Impact Scholarship Program By October 31

PR Newswire

TAMPA, Fla., Oct. 9, 2026

Sonic Tools USA to award five trade-specific toolsets and toolboxes in November, bringing a total of 10 scholarships awarded this year

TAMPA, Fla., Oct. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sonic Tools USA, a leading provider of professional-grade tool solutions and equipment, announced today that applications are open through Saturday, October 31, for the Fall 2026 Sonic Impact Scholarship Program.

 Sonic Tools USA to award five trade-specific toolsets and toolboxes in November to trade school students

The program is designed to equip the next generation of automotive, aviation, and manufacturing technicians with professional hand tools, empowering students to focus on their education and pursue careers in their chosen industry instead of the debt often accrued from investing in professional toolsets. In 2026, Sonic Tools USA is awarding a total of 10 scholarships: five recipients were selected in June, and five additional recipients will be chosen in November.

Each scholarship winner receives a comprehensive set of professional hand tools and a dedicated toolbox curated for their trade that's vetted by technical instructors, industry leaders, and Sonic Tools USA senior leadership. The trade-specific toolset options have listed retail values of up to $9,050 and come in Sonic Foam System (SFS) modules.

"Skilled and equipped new technicians make a vital impact across the aviation, automotive, and manufacturing industries, especially in the face of ongoing technician shortages," said Don Russell, director of marketing, Sonic Tools USA. "Our goal with the Sonic Impact Scholarship Program is to provide aspiring technicians with the tools of their trade from day one, helping them focus on their education and future careers while highlighting their demonstration of our core P.A.C.E. values."

Rewarding Students Who Exemplify P.A.C.E. Values
Designed to support technicians who live by the values of passion, accountability, collaboration, and experience, Sonic Tools USA is seeking applicants who share the following traits:

  • Passion: An unparalleled enthusiasm for one's career and education.
  • Accountability: Being dependable, caring about, and taking responsibility for one's work.
  • Collaboration: Working with others to achieve the best version of work.
  • Experience: Providing an 'unbeatable experience' for customers, peers, and co-workers.

How to Apply
Students committed to their trade can apply by submitting the following application materials on the Sonic Tools USA website by October 31:

  • Proof of enrollment in an automotive, aviation, or manufacturing trade school (class schedule or student ID).
  • Letter of recommendation from the student's instructor (including contact information).
  • 500-word essay on how the student exemplifies the values of P.A.C.E. while explaining "how I will make an Impact."
  • 60–90 second video on "how Sonic will make an impact on my career."

Sonic Tools USA will review and analyze all entries, and may choose to contact applicants for additional information. The organization reserves the right to contact their instructors. Sonic Tools USA will reach out directly to the five scholarship winners in November.

For more information, visit https://sonictoolsusa.com/scholarship/.

About Sonic Tools USA:
